solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Short match

definitions.meaning: ... can mean lacking, as in being a few pounds ... or short
a match is something that gives a ..., as in asking a smoker for a ...

explanation.surface: A brief sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means deficient in amount, and a struck match is a light for a cigarette or candle.

clue.text: Ridiculous proposal going forward, perhaps?

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy or ridiculous
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A daft suggestion is being pushed ahead regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that moving forward is just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is movement from place to place, of which advancing is one kind.

clue.text: One way matter may be sorted: action group firstly set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the letters are raised, so read from the bottom upwards
firstly asks for the opening letter of each of the words sorted, action and group

explanation.surface: Getting a pressure group organised is one way to sort out matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SAG, the first letters of 'sorted action group', upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid, liquid and gas are the classic states in which physical matter can exist.

clue.text: Chest: try stuffing instrument briefly inside

indicators.note: stuffing means the shortened instrument is packed inside the word for try

parts.note: to try someone's patience is to tax it

indicators.note: briefly means the word for the instrument is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A chest examination: try fitting the instrument inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of the instrument, and 'stuffing' packs what is left inside. 'Instrument' suggests a doctor's tool, but it is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the anatomical name for the part of the body enclosed by the ribs.

clue.text: Policeman I see dresses in fur — that sounds awful!

indicators.note: in means the whole group is then put inside the word for fur

parts.note: cony is rabbit fur

indicators.note: dresses means the exclamation wraps around the policeman like clothing

parts.note: ah is the exclamation of someone who now understands
cop is slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: An officer in a fur coat prompts a disapproving cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: 'dresses' wraps the exclamation round the officer, and 'in' then puts that inside the fur. Cony is an old word for rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cacophony is a harsh, discordant mixture of noises, so it is unpleasant to hear.

clue.text: Terrorist group go down having stolen uranium compound found in plant

indicators.note: having stolen means the two words take the symbol into their midst

parts.note: a cell is a small unit of a terrorist organisation
to go down in a contest is to lose
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Militants are defeated after seizing uranium from a power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having stolen' puts the uranium symbol between the two words. 'Plant' looks like a power station but means a growing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose is the carbohydrate polymer forming plant cell walls.

clue.text: Shape that is lovely

definitions.note: here a noun, an attractive person

parts.note: to shape something with a blade is to cut it
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A form that is beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive person, as is a lovely in the noun sense.

clue.text: Media affairs torrid under head of programming — that was careless!

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts the word for torrid below the first letter
head of asks for the opening letter of programming

parts.note: torrid means very hot
oops is what someone says after a clumsy mistake

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's steamy scandal at the top of the schedule was a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affairs' suggests romance, but here means arranged events.
explanation.definitionFit: Photo opportunities are staged events arranged so the press can take pictures.

clue.text: Forbidden, now spring's gone?

definitions.meaning: an area one is not allowed to enter is off limits
bounds are leaps or springs, so with them gone one has run out of them

explanation.surface: Banned, now that the season of spring has passed?
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like the season; it means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A place off limits is barred, and having no leaps left reads literally as lacking bounds.

clue.text: House given a choice of sturdy and weak foundations?

indicators.note: given means the pair of final letters is presented with the choice word set between them
in a down clue a word's foundation is its bottom, final letter, taken here from both sturdy and weak

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice between alternatives

explanation.surface: A building offered a pick between solid and flimsy footings.
explanation.walkthrough: House means a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: York was an English royal dynasty, ruling through Edward IV and Richard III.

clue.text: French dish: temptress primarily after person in suit

indicators.note: after places the first letter of temptress at the end
in puts the word for person inside the word for suit

parts.note: a lawsuit is a legal case
a soul is a person, as in not a soul about

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of temptress

explanation.surface: A seductress follows a man in a business suit, with French food in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing; it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassoulet is a slow-cooked stew of beans and meats from south-west France.

clue.text: Path with entrance to the rear, remote

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter, here sent to the back of the word for path

parts.note: a route is a path or way

explanation.surface: A walkway with a back door, far from anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer regions are the far-off, distant ones.

clue.text: In formula I get blunders: little holes in it?

indicators.note: blunders tells us the letters of the phrase stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A mathematician admits to errors in an equation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' rearranges IN FORMULA I GET.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy golf courses have small, short holes, so the game is built from tiny holes.

clue.text: Aberrant elder thrown in abyss

indicators.note: aberrant means straying from the normal course, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A deviant older person is cast into a deep pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aberrant' rearranges ELDER THROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld of myth is pictured as a bottomless pit beneath the earth.

clue.text: Partners, one's pals worryingly vulnerable to attack?

parts.note: in bridge West and East are partners

indicators.note: worryingly suggests the letters are troubled and tossed into a different order

explanation.surface: Your partners and friends are alarmingly exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worryingly' rearranges ONESPALS. Bridge seats players in pairs: North with South, East with West.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without arms cannot defend themselves, so is open to assault.

clue.text: I'm going towards being doubled up, after retirement

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing, so the doubled letters go backwards
being doubled up means the word for towards is written twice over

parts.note: at can mean towards, as in throwing a stone at a window

explanation.surface: Someone hunched over in pain as they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being doubled up' writes AT twice as ATAT; 'after retirement' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, said when someone is leaving.

clue.text: American brass cleaner welcoming American polish

definitions.note: a brass instrument designed in the US

indicators.note: welcoming means the cleaner takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: soap is a cleaner
to hone is to polish or refine

explanation.surface: An American metal polish that takes in more American polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the metal being cleaned; it is a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sousaphone is a large tuba made for John Philip Sousa's American marching bands.

clue.text: These days not much in some vacuous old tale

indicators.note: in places the two words inside the emptied word
vacuous means empty, so the word some loses its inside and keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: now means these days
a whit is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: Nowadays there is little to be found in some empty fairy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' empties the word some to its two outer letters, and 'in' puts the two synonyms between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The story of the princess and seven dwarfs is a traditional folk tale collected by the Brothers Grimm.

clue.text: Drug in operation worked, though not the first

indicators.note: worked means the remaining letters are kneaded into a new order
not the first means the opening letter of operation is dropped

explanation.surface: An anaesthetic worked in surgery, if not at the first attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not the first' drops the O of OPERATION, and 'worked' rearranges PERATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is an alkaloid from deadly nightshade, used medically to dilate pupils and steady the heart.

clue.text: Where soldiers were ordered to go too much

definitions.text: Where soldiers were ordered to go
definitions.meaning: in First World War trenches troops were ordered up and over the parapet to attack

explanation.surface: Where troops were sent, and it was excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Trench soldiers climbed over the parapet to attack, and the phrase now means excessive or exaggerated.

clue.text: That's a match, still!

definitions.meaning: in the children's card game ..., players shout this when two cards match
a still is a photograph, as is a quick photo

explanation.surface: Announcing a pair, motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game call greets matching cards, and a quick photograph is a still image.

clue.text: Wish we were here for wife

definitions.meaning: the postcard line wishing you were here, turned round: you long for our company
an informal word for a wife

explanation.surface: A holiday postcard message to the wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words and it is a request to long for our company.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is a colloquial term for a man's spouse.

clue.text: US president in dispute, PM joining club

indicators.note: in puts the word for dispute inside the pair
joining means the prime minister is attached after the club

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club
Harold Wilson was a British prime minister
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A US president is at odds as a prime minister joins a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' gives WOODWILSON; 'in' puts ROW between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodrow Wilson was the 28th President of the United States, in office during the First World War.

clue.text: Ultimately joyous, supremely uplifting puzzle

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the letters are raised and read upwards
ultimately asks for the final letter of joyous

parts.note: uber, from German, is used as a prefix meaning supremely

explanation.surface: A puzzle that is joyful and hugely inspiring in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns SUBER (S from 'Ultimately joyous' plus UBER) upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Old sovereign tender, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word for tender is said aloud to give a name that sounds the same

parts.note: to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: An old gold coin offered as legal tender?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' and 'tender' suggest money; Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, who built Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, so he is a long-dead monarch.

clue.text: After a review, I declare myself the official physicist

indicators.note: a review is a looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I'm declares who I am, so it is short for I am
ref is short for referee, the match official

explanation.surface: After looking things over, I state that I am the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a review' turns IMREF round.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Fermi was the Italian-American scientist who built the first nuclear reactor.

clue.text: Butterfly is full colour

parts.note: a cup that brims is full to the top
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A butterfly is full of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a sulphur-yellow butterfly common in Europe.

clue.text: Not so bad hugging a tree

indicators.note: hugging means the word for not so bad wraps around the letter

parts.note: OK means passable, not too bad

explanation.surface: Tree-hugging is not such a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak is a common broadleaf tree that grows acorns.

clue.text: Appellation on envelope erased, send off without name

indicators.note: off means the remaining letters are put out of order
without means the letter for name is taken out of the words

explanation.surface: The name on an envelope has been rubbed out, so send it off unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes N from ERASED SEND, and 'off' rearranges ERASEDSED.
explanation.definitionFit: The recipient's name heads the address written on a letter's envelope.

clue.text: Malevolent character, US president once on board?

indicators.note: on, with board, means the president is put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, so on board means aboard a ship
Ike was the nickname of President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A former president aboard ship is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The villain of Oliver Twist is a violent, menacing figure in Dickens's novel.
